items.summary: Would you be willing to pay to use AI features built into your phone?
items.body:

Mobile

Here's how much OnePlus could charge you for using ColorOS 17's AI features

Would you be willing to pay to use AI features built into your phone?

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 3:26 AM ET

•

•

Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• OPPO has introduced three monthly AI subscription tiers for ColorOS 17 in India.

• The plans range from around $3 to $10 and will offer up to 100,000 credits per month.

• Only Live Translation, AI Photo Agent, and Transcription features will use credits, while other AI features remain free.

OnePlus recently confirmed that it will start imposing usage limits on some AI features in ColorOS 17. Users will have a free usage allowance, after which they can either pay for more usage or wait for their allowance to reset. However, the company hadn’t confirmed price details just yet. Well, we’re getting a clearer idea of its plans now.

According to a post on X by user Ashok Mor, OPPO has started offering subscription-based AI plans for ColorOS 17. There are three subscription tiers, per their post:

• Basic: Rs. 289/month (~$3/month) for 20,000 credits

• Pro: Rs. 579/month (~$6/month) for 50,000 credits

• Ultra: Rs. 959/month (~$10/month) for 100,000 credits

These credits are reportedly shared across three AI features: Live Translation, AI Photo Agent, and Transcription. Based on the post, the Basic plan will get you roughly 50 Photo Agent uses or 100 minutes of translation. The Pro plan bumps that up to 125 uses or 250 minutes, while the Ultra plan offers around 250 uses or 500 minutes.

@_techibee / X

You can also buy top-up credits if you run out of your monthly quota, with credit packs starting at Rs. 189 (~$2) for 10,000 credits. These credits are valid for one year. OPPO also seems to be running a limited-time offer that gives users 10,000 free credits per month for one year, so users can experiment with the AI features before deciding whether to subscribe.

Based on the screenshots in the post, it seems only the three AI features listed above will use AI credits. Other AI features in ColorOS 17 could remain available for free, at least for now. Neither OnePlus nor OPPO has officially announced a rollout or confirmed pricing for other regions. We have reached out to both companies for a statement and will update this post when we hear back.

items.title: Oura is dropping Android 11 support in December, and users risk losing health data
items.summary: Upgrading after the deadline won't bring back your health history.
items.body:

Wearables and health

Oura is dropping Android 11 support in December, and users risk losing health data

Upgrading after the deadline won't bring back your health history.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 3:14 AM ET

•

•

Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Oura will officially drop support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026.

• Users who don’t upgrade to Android 12 or newer by the deadline risk losing their historical health data.

• Those who remain on Android 11 may retain access to some limited historical app features.

One of the biggest benefits of wearing an Oura Ring is that the longer you use it, the more you learn about your health. From personalized annual health recaps to long-term blood pressure trends, many of Oura’s features become more useful as you build up months or even years of health data. However, some Android users could soon lose access to that history simply because of the phone they use.

Oura has updated its Android software updates support page to reveal that it will discontinue support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. Starting on that date, you’ll need a phone running Android 12 or newer to continue enjoying the full Oura app experience.

Oura will drop support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. If you are using an Android device, be sure to update to Android 12 or higher to ensure no loss of data or features. If you decide not to upgrade, you may still be able to use some limited historical Oura App features. Please note that if you do upgrade your smartphone system later, your historical Oura data will not carry over.

What’s particularly concerning is that this goes beyond missing out on new features and app updates. Oura warns that users who stick with Android 11 may retain access to some limited historical app features, but upgrading their phone’s operating system later will not bring their historical Oura data with them.

Essentially, putting off that software update could cost you years of sleep, activity, and recovery history.

Android 11 is now more than six years old, and Oura isn’t alone in moving away from older Android versions. Earlier this month, Google raised Android Auto’s minimum requirement to Android 11. But Oura is taking things a step further.

If your phone is still running Android 11, you should check for available software updates before December 8. Those whose phones are no longer eligible for OS updates may need to switch to a newer device. Oura also lets you export your health data through its Membership Hub, so it’s worth downloading a copy before the deadline.

items.title: Samsung phones can soon nudge you when you miss your usual charging window
items.summary: This charging reminder feature could even refer to your calendar entries for more personalized alerts.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

Samsung phones can soon nudge you when you miss your usual charging window

This charging reminder feature could even refer to your calendar entries for more personalized alerts.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 3:11 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Samsung’s One UI 9.5 beta can apparently tell you when you’ve missed your usual charging time.

• This alert will show up in the Settings menu and will also show how many hours of battery life you have left.

• This feature could be very useful if you’re forgetful or busy.

Samsung recently launched the One UI 9.5 beta program, allowing Galaxy S26 owners to get their hands on the latest software before the stable release. We’ve already uncovered plenty of features, but it looks like the company has a convenient charging-related feature up its sleeve.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We’ve dug into the Device Care app (v13.9.00.12) in One UI 9.5 and discovered that Samsung phones could soon issue an alert when you’ve missed your usual charging time. We can confirm that this alert will appear when the battery is at 20-30% capacity, your phone isn’t charging, and power-saving modes are disabled. Check out the string below.

Code

<string name="suggest_appbar_charging_description">You missed your usual charging time.</string>

We’ve also uncovered strings (seen below) which show that the alert could use events in your default calendar for context. More specifically, the alert could mention that your battery might be low for a workout, movie, meeting, or show/concert at a given time. If you don’t have a matching calendar event, then the feature will fall back to the alert message seen in the string above.

Code

<string name="suggest_appbar_exercise_description">Battery may be low for your workout at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_meeting_description">Battery may be low for your meeting at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_movie_description">Battery may be low for your movie at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_performance_description">Battery may be low for your %1$s at %2$s.</string>

So how does this actually work? Well, you’ll first need to enable Samsung’s personalized suggestions option and have a device with One UI 9.5. The phone will then identify your preferred charging window by learning from four weeks of charging history, as retained by the Smart suggestions app. The device will then check if the current hour falls within this preferred charging window, and display the alert if this is the case. The code suggests that if you dismiss the alert, it won’t come back again for 24 hours, even if all other conditions are met. Oddly enough, we also found evidence that Samsung can remotely turn off this card.

There’s no country check, while the evidence we’ve uncovered also suggests that it won’t be exclusive to the Galaxy S27 series. So this charging alert could potentially come to older Galaxy phones in many markets.

What could these charging alerts look like?

SamMobile also posted a screenshot showing off this alert. It’s unclear whether this feature is available in some capacity or if the outlet manually enabled it by tinkering with the software. Check out the image below.

SamMobile

This notification apparently pops up at the top of the Settings menu. It also includes a graphic showing how many hours of battery life you have left and how much usage time you’ll gain if you enable battery-saving mode.

I can see this proactive alert being very useful for people who either forget to charge their phones or those who are very busy. That battery life graphic should also help you make up your mind about whether you need to charge your device straight away.

Either way, this charging alert seems like a very sensible addition to One UI 9.5. We hope other Android OEMs copy Samsung and implement this in their own software skins.

items.summary: TCL CSOT showed off the future of display tech at DTC 2026.
items.body:

General technology

TCL CSOT unveils APEX and IJP OLED breakthroughs for the AI era at DTC 2026

TCL CSOT showed off the future of display tech at DTC 2026.

Brought to you by TCL CSOT

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 2:56 AM ET

•

TCL CSOT

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

A screen has a big impact on how a device feels to use. It determines how crisp text looks on your laptop, how smoothly fast-moving games appear on your monitor, how long your phone lasts on a charge, and whether the person next to you on the train can read your screen. OLED screens, in particular, need a lot of precision to manufacture, which is why they’re most often found only in higher-end phones, laptops, monitors, and tablets.

TCL CSOT, which makes and develops displays for many device manufacturers, is working on a method to build OLED panels by printing the materials onto them, which could help OLED get into more products.

At DTC 2026, its annual Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference in Wuhan, China, on November 13, TCL CSOT showcased its latest display tech: inkjet-printed OLED, a 500Hz gaming monitor, a 115-inch 16K screen that shows 3D without glasses, and more. They also took Android Authority on a tour of the Wuhan factory and the t12 production line, where they’re working on the IJP OLED. Here’s what you need to know.

How inkjet-printed OLED works

TCL CSOT

IJP OLED stands for inkjet-printed OLED. While traditional OLED manufacturing uses processes to deposit organic materials onto the display, IJP OLED uses specialized printers to place those materials precisely where they’re needed. The idea is similar to using a home inkjet printer, but the “ink” is made of organic materials that form a working OLED panel.

Printing the materials this way helps reduce waste and potentially lower manufacturing costs, which is a significant advantage for bringing OLED to a wider range of products in the future.

It also offers a picture-quality benefit. IJP OLED uses TCL CSOT’s Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement, with separate red, green, and blue subpixels arranged in stripes. This design delivers sharper text and noticeably reduces color fringing around the edges of text and graphics compared with a conventional OLED panel.

TCL CSOT

Interview with Weiran Cao, Ph.D, at DTC 2026

With IJP OLED, we can reach 163 PPI on a 27-inch 4K display. For gaming displays, it can reach 218 PPI, with a 0.03 millisecond response time. People read a lot of text on monitors and laptops, so this is a benefit users can see every day.Weiran Cao, Ph.D, General Manager of IJP-OLED Middle Platform of TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT has already begun mass-producing IJP OLED panels, and several partner devices using this tech were featured at DTC 2026. The Lenovo Legion R9000P has a 16-inch IJP OLED panel with a 2,560×1,600 resolution, a 240Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3 coverage. Meanwhile, Lenovo’s ThinkVision P27UL-40 is the company’s first IJP OLED monitor for commercial use, with a 27-inch 4K display and 99% DCI-P3 coverage. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ and MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 also use TCL CSOT’s printed panels.

TCL CSOT has also introduced two new 14-inch IJP OLED notebook panels. One is less than 0.66mm thick, weighs under 66g, and has a reflectance of less than 1%. The other eliminates the cover glass, using a hardened polarizer with an 8H rating instead, but it still feels like glass to the touch, whether you use a finger or a stylus.

A 500Hz gaming monitor and a 115-inch 3D TV display

TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch QHD gaming monitor featuring an IJP OLED panel with an oxide backplane, and supporting refresh rates of up to 500Hz. TCL CSOT says it’s the first display to use in-panel compensation for high refresh rates. It helps maintain picture quality and runs in real time in the background, so there’s no need for the periodic power-off cycles used by conventional methods.

Real Stripe RGB keeps edges sharp, with a response time under 1ms. The 500Hz refresh rate is designed for competitive gaming, keeping moving targets in fast-paced shooters crisp and easy to track.

TCL CSOT

The 115-inch display has a native 16K resolution of 15,360×7,680, and TCL CSOT says it is the world’s highest image quality 16K 2D/3D-compatible light-field TV display. Its light-field optical architecture addresses the viewing-angle limitations of conventional glasses-free 3D, offering a 90-degree viewing angle or more, extended depth of field, and support for multiple viewers, so you don’t have to sit in one specific spot. The 3D light-field resolution reaches up to 8K, and the screen can switch between 2D and 3D, with TCL CSOT claiming there’s no loss in 2D picture quality.

The recommended viewing distance is 2–4m (6.5–13ft), making it well suited for private theatres, digital museums, interactive gaming, and premium showrooms. It’s an impressive display, though it’s unlikely to find its way into living rooms anytime soon.

More efficient and more private mobile displays

TCL CSOT

The 6.36-inch blue phosphorescent OLED may have been one of the most practical displays at DTC 2026. TCL CSOT says it’s the first smartphone OLED display to use a blue phosphorescent material system, which they say delivers roughly 40% higher luminous efficiency and around 20% lower electroluminescent power consumption at the same brightness.

The display is a major power draw, so the battery-life improvements are definitely exciting. Paired with the larger batteries introduced in newer handsets, more efficient screens could significantly increase the time you can use your device between charges. TCL CSOT is also working to refine materials and manufacturing processes to extend device lifetimes and bring blue phosphorescent displays to more devices.

TCL CSOT

The World’s First Full-Angle Lossless Privacy OLED Tablet Display(10.95″) helps keep your screen private from people nearby. Its dual-pixel architecture and pixel-level light-path control provide 360-degree active privacy while keeping the view clear from the front.

APEX and AI for Real

TCL CSOT

All of these technologies are part of APEX, TCL CSOT’s advanced display technology brand, created with picture quality, eye comfort, and sustainability in mind. APEX is built on four pillars: Amazing Display Experience, Protective of Eye Health, Eco-friendly to Build and Use, and Unlimited Imaginative Potential.

AI for Real was another major focus at DTC 2026. TCL’s strategy is to bring AI out of the lab and into everyday life. For TCL CSOT, a key part of that vision is Display for AI — advancing display technology so AI-powered devices can deliver a better experience. Whatever an AI assistant does on your phone or laptop, the screen is where you see the results and respond. That means better displays can make AI features feel more useful in your day-to-day life.

Know more about TCL CSOT at DTC 2026

TCL CSOT

At DTC 2026, TCL CSOT showed off its progress on several fronts. IJP OLED is moving beyond the demo stage and toward mass production, while gaming panels are advancing toward 500Hz. The company also showcased a 115-inch glasses-free 3D screen, along with new mobile panels that use less power and help keep your screen private. Bringing these efforts together is AI, which is helping TCL CSOT design displays much faster. And the great news is that many of these features are already in everyday use.

TCL CSOT makes panels for other device makers, so you can find its technology in products from a range of brands. IJP OLED is already featured in Lenovo and MSI laptops and monitors showcased at DTC 2026. The other displays are currently technology demonstrations, with no retail timelines announced yet. You can find more information about TCL CSOT’s display technology on its website.

It also offers a picture-quality benefit. IJP OLED uses TCL CSOT’s Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement, with separate red, green, and blue subpixels arranged in stripes. This design delivers sharper text and noticeably reduces color fringing around the edges of text and graphics compared with a conventional OLED panel.
TCL CSOT
Interview with Weiran Cao, Ph.D, at DTC 2026

With IJP OLED, we can reach 163 PPI on a 27-inch 4K display. For gaming displays, it can reach 218 PPI, with a 0.03 millisecond response time. People read a lot of text on monitors and laptops, so this is a benefit users can see every day.Weiran Cao, Ph.D, General Manager of IJP-OLED Middle Platform of TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT has already begun mass-producing IJP OLED panels, and several partner devices using this tech were featured at DTC 2026. The Lenovo Legion R9000P has a 16-inch IJP OLED panel with a 2,560×1,600 resolution, a 240Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3 coverage. Meanwhile, Lenovo’s ThinkVision P27UL-40 is the company’s first IJP OLED monitor for commercial use, with a 27-inch 4K display and 99% DCI-P3 coverage. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ and MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 also use TCL CSOT’s printed panels.

TCL CSOT has also introduced two new 14-inch IJP OLED notebook panels. One is less than 0.66mm thick, weighs under 66g, and has a reflectance of less than 1%. The other eliminates the cover glass, using a hardened polarizer with an 8H rating instead, but it still feels like glass to the touch, whether you use a finger or a stylus.
A 500Hz gaming monitor and a 115-inch 3D TV display
TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch QHD gaming monitor featuring an IJP OLED panel with an oxide backplane, and supporting refresh rates of up to 500Hz. TCL CSOT says it’s the first display to use in-panel compensation for high refresh rates. It helps maintain picture quality and runs in real time in the background, so there’s no need for the periodic power-off cycles used by conventional methods.
Real Stripe RGB keeps edges sharp, with a response time under 1ms. The 500Hz refresh rate is designed for competitive gaming, keeping moving targets in fast-paced shooters crisp and easy to track.
TCL CSOT

The 115-inch display has a native 16K resolution of 15,360×7,680, and TCL CSOT says it is the world’s highest image quality 16K 2D/3D-compatible light-field TV display. Its light-field optical architecture addresses the viewing-angle limitations of conventional glasses-free 3D, offering a 90-degree viewing angle or more, extended depth of field, and support for multiple viewers, so you don’t have to sit in one specific spot. The 3D light-field resolution reaches up to 8K, and the screen can switch between 2D and 3D, with TCL CSOT claiming there’s no loss in 2D picture quality.

The recommended viewing distance is 2–4m (6.5–13ft), making it well suited for private theatres, digital museums, interactive gaming, and premium showrooms. It’s an impressive display, though it’s unlikely to find its way into living rooms anytime soon.
More efficient and more private mobile displays
TCL CSOT

The 6.36-inch blue phosphorescent OLED may have been one of the most practical displays at DTC 2026. TCL CSOT says it’s the first smartphone OLED display to use a blue phosphorescent material system, which they say delivers roughly 40% higher luminous efficiency and around 20% lower electroluminescent power consumption at the same brightness.

The display is a major power draw, so the battery-life improvements are definitely exciting. Paired with the larger batteries introduced in newer handsets, more efficient screens could significantly increase the time you can use your device between charges. TCL CSOT is also working to refine materials and manufacturing processes to extend device lifetimes and bring blue phosphorescent displays to more devices.
TCL CSOT

The World’s First Full-Angle Lossless Privacy OLED Tablet Display(10.95″) helps keep your screen private from people nearby. Its dual-pixel architecture and pixel-level light-path control provide 360-degree active privacy while keeping the view clear from the front.
APEX and AI for Real
TCL CSOT

All of these technologies are part of APEX, TCL CSOT’s advanced display technology brand, created with picture quality, eye comfort, and sustainability in mind. APEX is built on four pillars: Amazing Display Experience, Protective of Eye Health, Eco-friendly to Build and Use, and Unlimited Imaginative Potential.

AI for Real was another major focus at DTC 2026. TCL’s strategy is to bring AI out of the lab and into everyday life. For TCL CSOT, a key part of that vision is Display for AI — advancing display technology so AI-powered devices can deliver a better experience. Whatever an AI assistant does on your phone or laptop, the screen is where you see the results and respond. That means better displays can make AI features feel more useful in your day-to-day life.
Know more about TCL CSOT at DTC 2026
TCL CSOT

At DTC 2026, TCL CSOT showed off its progress on several fronts. IJP OLED is moving beyond the demo stage and toward mass production, while gaming panels are advancing toward 500Hz. The company also showcased a 115-inch glasses-free 3D screen, along with new mobile panels that use less power and help keep your screen private. Bringing these efforts together is AI, which is helping TCL CSOT design displays much faster. And the great news is that many of these features are already in everyday use.

TCL CSOT makes panels for other device makers, so you can find its technology in products from a range of brands. IJP OLED is already featured in Lenovo and MSI laptops and monitors showcased at DTC 2026. The other displays are currently technology demonstrations, with no retail timelines announced yet. You can find more information about TCL CSOT’s display technology on its website.

In the U.S., Apple's terms and conditions say the promotion begins on November 27 at 12 a.m. Pacific Time and ends on November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. During the shopping event, customers can get an Apple gift card with the purchase of an eligible product at an Apple Store, in the Apple Store app, and on Apple.com. However, the gift card can only be used towards future purchases, and higher immediate discounts on Apple products are frequently available at Amazon and other resellers. In the U.S., Apple is offering gift cards worth up to $300 with the purchase of an eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, Beats Pill speaker, Apple Pencil Pro, and select Magic Keyboards for iPads. For the first time ever, Apple is also offering a $25 gift card with select third-party accessories from brands including Anker, Belkin, Mophie, Nimble, Rains, and Twelve South. As usual, many of Apple's newer products are excluded from the offer, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, MacBook Neo, latest models of the iPad mini, Apple TV 4K, iMac, and Mac Studio, and more. quote.text: 三星、海力士、美光遭美国集体诉讼，被指借 HBM 转型操纵 DRAM 价格  诉状的核心论点在于：三星、SK海力士与美光凭借其在全球DRAM市场的寡头地位，在协同推进向HBM转型的同时，以这一战略调整为由大幅削减DDR3、DDR4等商用内存的产能，人为制造供给收缩。导致商用DRAM价格在过去四年间累计上涨约700%，对全球消费电子及商业IT采购造成广泛冲击。 ‎https://wallstreetcn.com/~

comments.text: 这一定都是阿共仔的阴谋.jpg

三家企业辩称，中国厂商正在扩大DDR4内存生产，给它们带来竞争压力，因此，逐步退出DDR4是正常的商业选择。

原告却认为，中国厂商当时所占的全球DRAM产能只有约5%，甚至更低，不足以解释三家企业几乎同时退出DDR4的决定。

更有意思的是，根据长鑫科技公开披露的材料，早在2024年底，长鑫就已经停止生产自有DDR4产品，开始向DDR5升级。而三星、SK海力士和美光，直到2025年4月至6月才相继宣布逐步退出主流DDR4生产。‎
